title: The authority in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19F(a) for a registered pharmacist to prescribe and dispense hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives
subtopic: Statutory authority for pharmacist contraceptive prescribing
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19F(a), as struck out and replaced by St. 2025, c. 14, s. 39, notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, a registered pharmacist may: (i) prescribe and dispense hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives to any person, regardless of whether the person has evidence of a previous prescription from a primary care practitioner or reproductive health care practitioner for a hormonal contraceptive patch or self-administered oral hormonal contraceptive; and (ii) prescribe, dispense and administer medications used for the treatment and prevention of human immunodeficiency virus and sexually transmitted infections as defined by the department. Section 19F was inserted in chapter 94C by St. 2023, c. 28, s. 42; section 115 of that act provides that, except as otherwise specified, the act shall take effect as of July 1, 2023, and the act specifies no other date for section 42. Chapter 14 of the Acts of 2025 was declared an emergency law in its preamble and was approved on August 5, 2025. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1, 'Department' means the department of public health.
exam_relevance: Tests who holds the statutory authority, which contraceptive products it reaches, that evidence of a previous practitioner prescription is not a precondition, and that the 2025 rewrite of subsection (a) placed the HIV and sexually transmitted infection authority in a separate clause.

authority.name: Prescription and dispensation of hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives by registered pharmacists
Acts of 2025, Chapter 14, replacing subsection (a) of section 19F of chapter 94C
Acts of 2023, Chapter 28, inserting section 19F in chapter 94C

common_confusions: Treating a previous prescription from a primary care practitioner or reproductive health care practitioner as a precondition; subsection (a)(i) authorizes prescribing and dispensing regardless of whether the person has evidence of one.
Reading the contraceptive authority in subsection (a)(i) as reaching products other than hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives.

Reading subsection (a) without the 2025 rewrite, which added clause (ii) for medications used for the treatment and prevention of human immunodeficiency virus and sexually transmitted infections as defined by the department.
verification_notes: Read M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19F and s. 1 on malegislature.gov, and St. 2023, c. 28 (sections 42 and 115, the emergency preamble and the approval line) and St. 2025, c. 14 (section 39, the emergency preamble and the approval line) on malegislature.gov, on 2026-09-16. When read, the General Laws page for s. 19F displayed subsection (a) as a single clause without the words substituted by St. 2025, c. 14, s. 39, so the current wording of subsection (a) is taken from the session law.
